clue.text: Quarrel over arms proliferation?

parts.note: a falling-out is a quarrel, and one about atomic weapons spreading is read as the radioactive aftermath of a bomb

explanation.surface: Diplomats argue bitterly about the spread of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a row between nations, but the phrase it describes is the radioactive dust that settles after an atomic explosion; its second word also hints at a falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: a quarrel is a falling-out, and the arms in question are atomic ones.

clue.text: Mortgaged estate?

parts.note: buying on credit is British slang 'on the never-never', and an estate is land, so a mortgaged estate becomes the fantasy island of Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A property bought with a loan from the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, hire purchase is nicknamed 'the never-never' because the payments seem endless; the fairy-tale home of Peter Pan is reached by reading a mortgaged estate that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: land bought on hire purchase, which also names Peter Pan's imaginary island.

clue.text: Car (not one around recently)

parts.note: a motor model that Ford stopped making, so none has been seen on the road lately

explanation.surface: A motor of a kind rarely seen these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Cortina was a hugely popular British family saloon, discontinued in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Cortina is a car model no longer in production, hence not seen around recently.

clue.text: A wild rose can be elegant in flower

indicators.note: the letters of the next two words can be turned into something new, a rearrangement signal

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hedgerow rose looks graceful when it blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals that ELEGANT and IN are rearranged; 'flower' simply rounds off the surface, echoing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is another name for the sweetbriar, a wild rose of European hedgerows.

clue.text: Old catalogues brought up the street to the Steptoes

indicators.note: to means one piece is attached after the other

parts.note: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing the letters up reverses them

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Junk dealers collect old mail-order catalogues from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Steptoe and Son was a British TV comedy about two rag-and-bone men (junk collectors). 'brought up' turns ST into TS beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragment is an archaic word for a catalogue or list, as in a ragman roll.

clue.text: Battle — one taking place in West London suburb

indicators.note: the numeral is set within the suburb, as an event takes place within a location

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in a London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a suburb in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is a military engagement, a synonym for battle.

clue.text: Artist for the underground?

definitions.meaning: the English painter L. S. ..., known for industrial scenes
read as low plus RY, the abbreviation for railway: a low railway, an underground

explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of industrial scenes; his name read as LOW + RY (railway) gives an underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry was the Salford painter famous for matchstick figures, and his name punningly suggests a low railway.

clue.text: Of doubtful age, like an old maid

definitions.meaning: lacking a date, so its age is uncertain
an old maid, an unmarried woman, has jokingly never been taken out on a date

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as un-dated: never asked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a date means of uncertain age; humorously, a spinster never courted has not been dated.

clue.text: A craftsman, nothing other than mass-producer

indicators.note: a producer makes something new out of materials, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artisan who is nothing but a factory-line manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producer' (from 'mass-producer') signals rearranging O with OTHER THAN MASS. Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a celebrated Georgian cabinet-maker and furniture designer, so a craftsman.

clue.text: Signal carrying little weight

definitions.meaning: a flare fired from a pistol as a signal, named after its inventor Very

explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a coloured signal flare; read as two words it means of minimal weight.

clue.text: Germany in with broadness of beam

indicators.note: in places the country code inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German boat is noted for being wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is breadth, and a ship's beam is its width at the broadest point.

clue.text: Rule about unknown

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
IGN is the dictionary abbreviation for ignotus, Latin for unknown

explanation.surface: A regulation concerning something nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a period of rule by a monarch, so the noun means rule.

clue.text: English check over comfortable environment

indicators.note: over places one piece beside the other in the charade

parts.note: cosy means comfortable
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: An English inspector examines a pleasant setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a community of organisms and its surroundings, an environment in the ecological sense.

clue.text: To get slim I returned and had a meal

parts.note: returned is read as 'came back', so the word came is written backwards
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: I came home and ate, which is no way to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius reads 'returned' as 'came back': the word came written backwards. A solver hunting for a reversed I will find nothing there.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make or become abnormally thin, an extreme form of getting slim.

clue.text: Suit in which to give emphasis

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
the idiom 'in ...' means to a great degree, emphatically

explanation.definitionFit: Spades is a card suit, and doing something 'in spades' means doing it emphatically.

clue.text: Do the perverted gape there?

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether lechers stare at a certain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGE THREE was the Sun newspaper's page of topless models, notorious in Britain; 'perverted' rearranges GAPE THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue: the tabloid page of topless pin-ups is where leering readers would gape.

clue.text: Creature seen in playtime to drink up

parts.note: the word playtime is read as T (time) seen inside PLAY

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are reversed

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An animal appears at break time to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playtime' is split as PLAY with T (time) seen inside, so 'seen in' belongs to that piece rather than signalling hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal, a creature indeed.

clue.text: Directions limiting poet producing epic verse

indicators.note: the two directions bound the poet on either side

parts.note: E (east) twice gives two compass directions
Alexander Pope was an English poet

explanation.surface: Instructions restrict a poet who writes long narrative poems.
explanation.definitionFit: An epopee is an epic poem, or epic poetry as a genre.

clue.text: Maybe free-range, like men taken to state penitentiary, almost

indicators.note: taken to means the next piece is joined on after

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: Like soldiers carted off to a state prison, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for prison; 'almost' drops its K. 'like' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is farmed without chemicals, and free-range is an example of such a method.

clue.text: Goal with rich type to be one of the few in charge

definitions.text: one of the few in charge

indicators.note: type as a verb means to set out, as in printing, so the letters are set again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy person aims to join the ruling elite.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is a member of an oligarchy, government by a small group.

clue.text: Squirmed audibly, one having lost ball

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: squirmed means wriggled

explanation.surface: Someone fidgets out loud after losing a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A riggald is a dialect word for an animal (or man) with an undescended or missing testicle, so the 'ball' is not a sports ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A riggald, or ridgel, is an imperfectly castrated animal with one testicle remaining.

clue.text: Gay girl on the bottle

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman has taken to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gay in its older sense means merry and light-hearted, a synonym for jovial.

clue.text: One to get all our members irritated?

definitions.text: One to get all our members irritated?

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken yob annoys everyone in the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges GET ALL OUR; the whole clue describes a drunken hooligan who annoys club members.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish young drinker is exactly the sort who would irritate every member.

clue.text: A sage, Irish from first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front to the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wise man from Ireland goes from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or seer, so the word means a wise man.

clue.text: What animal classically rules over?

indicators.note: over means the Latin word is turned back to front

parts.note: regit is Latin, the classical language, for he rules

explanation.surface: A question asking which beast is king.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the big cat, a predatory animal of Asia.

clue.text: Idiots in Oz, not from a grammar school

parts.note: non is a prefix meaning not
GS stands for grammar school

explanation.surface: Australian fools who did not go to a selective school.
explanation.definitionFit: Nong is Australian slang for a fool, so idiots in Oz.

clue.text: Bring worker into the country, which is not to be ignored

definitions.meaning: to import an ant, a worker insect, from abroad

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as IMPORT ANT; 'which is' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important matters and must not be ignored; split, it means importing an ant.

clue.text: A viral infection is abroad, lengthwise in lower leg

parts.note: a chill is a cold, a viral infection
est is French for is
end-on means lengthwise, with the end facing forward

explanation.surface: A virus is spreading overseas, affecting the shin lengthwise.
explanation.walkthrough: EST is French for 'is'; END-ON means lengthwise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscle to the heel bone, in the lower leg.
